name: What are the signs my bathroom needs a full gut instead of a cosmetic update?

mainEntity.name: How can I tell if my bathroom needs a full demolition and rebuild instead of just new finishes?
mainEntity.text: How can I tell if my bathroom needs a full demolition and rebuild instead of just new finishes?

acceptedAnswer.text: A cosmetic update works when the structure and systems are sound. A full gut becomes the smarter choice when the bathroom has repeated leaks, mold odors, soft floors, damaged framing, failing tile systems, or very outdated plumbing and electrical work. If the layout is cramped or the current shower and tub are badly positioned, rebuilding from the studs may be the most efficient long-term solution. A good contractor should inspect for signs of hidden damage before recommending a finish-only update. In older homes, the cost difference between a partial fix and a proper rebuild may be smaller than expected once concealed repairs are counted. The key question is not whether the room looks tired, but whether its underlying systems are reliable enough to keep.
acceptedAnswer.description: A full gut is usually needed when there is active leaking, major mold, rotten subflooring, outdated plumbing, unsafe wiring, failed shower waterproofing, or a layout that no longer works. If several of these problems are present, cosmetic updates will not solve the underlying issue.
